atomic_claim: There were 54,699 U.S. medical-school applicants in the 2025 cycle.
limitations: Applicant count is not the number accepted and cannot yield a personal probability.

atomic_claim: There were 23,440 first-year U.S. medical-school matriculants in 2025.
limitations: Matriculation is downstream of acceptance; the count is not an acceptance count.

atomic_claim: The 2025 matriculant-to-applicant ratio was 42.9% (23,440 / 54,699); this is a derived system ratio, not a personal acceptance probability.
limitations: Applicants may receive multiple acceptances; matriculation differs from acceptance.
exact_locator: Calculated from AAMC counts in E001 and E002

atomic_claim: Mean GPA among 2025 applicants was 3.67.
limitations: No distribution or conditional acceptance rate supplied in this release.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, applicant profile paragraph

atomic_claim: Mean GPA among 2025 matriculants was 3.81.
limitations: Matriculant mean is not a cutoff and is affected by selection and enrollment choices.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, applicant profile paragraph

atomic_claim: Mean MCAT among 2025 applicants was 506.3.
limitations: No distribution or conditional acceptance rate supplied in this release.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, applicant profile paragraph

atomic_claim: Mean MCAT among 2025 matriculants was 512.1.
limitations: Matriculant mean is not a cutoff and is affected by selection and enrollment choices.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, applicant profile paragraph

atomic_claim: The 2025 matriculating class reported more than 16.8 million cumulative community-service hours.
limitations: Self-reported cumulative hours among matriculants only; exact total stated as greater than 16.8 million.

atomic_claim: The 2025 matriculating class averaged 717 community-service hours per student.
limitations: Mean only; likely right-skewed; no applicant comparator, percentile, or adjusted effect.
relevance_to_trajectory: Broad benchmark; not a target or threshold

atomic_claim: First-time applicants constituted 76.5% of 2025 applicants.
limitations: Does not estimate the acceptance effect of reapplication.

atomic_claim: First-generation applicants constituted 13.8% of 2025 applicants.
limitations: Context characteristic; not a permissible standalone probability boost.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, socioeconomic context paragraph

atomic_claim: First-generation students constituted 10.7% of 2025 matriculants.
limitations: Applicant and matriculant shares are not an adjusted admissions effect.
exact_locator: AAMC 2025 enrollment news, socioeconomic context paragraph

atomic_claim: Applicants older than 30 constituted 2.6% of 2025 matriculants.
limitations: No acceptance effect; age should not be transformed into a demographic boost.

atomic_claim: Among 153,664 first-time U.S. MD applicants in 2017-2020, 45.3% were accepted.
limitations: Study period predates the current cycle; restricted to first-time applicants.

atomic_claim: 37.0% of first-time applicants reported scholarly activities.
limitations: Binary indicator combines publications, conferences, and posters; no hours, duration, role, or quality.

atomic_claim: 74.3% of first-time applicants reported shadowing.
limitations: Binary indicator; no hours, specialties, duration, or adjusted marginal effect reported in the extracted result.

atomic_claim: Unadjusted acceptance among first-generation applicants was 37.9%.
population: First-time U.S. MD applicants; first-generation subgroup
limitations: Confounded by academic and experiential differences; not a model input.

atomic_claim: Unadjusted acceptance among applicants from households below $75,000 was 39.6%.
population: First-time U.S. MD applicants; low-income subgroup
limitations: Income definition and study-period context; confounded and not a standalone probability boost.

atomic_claim: Each one-point MCAT increase was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.19 for acceptance.
covariates: Science GPA quintile, activities, and demographic/context variables
limitations: Odds ratio is not a probability increment; nonlinear probability depends on baseline and covariates.

atomic_claim: Highest science-GPA quintile was associated with adjusted odds ratio 7.15 for acceptance versus the lowest quintile.
limitations: Quintile boundaries are dataset-specific; odds ratio is not a probability multiplier.

atomic_claim: Nonmedical employment showed adjusted odds ratio 1.01 for acceptance.
limitations: Binary indicator omits hours, economic necessity, role, duration, and quality; CI includes 1.
relevance_to_trajectory: Evidence against a generic employment bonus

atomic_claim: After adjustment, first-generation status had odds ratio 1.14 for acceptance in the primary model.
limitations: Model is not a policy recommendation; interaction specification changed the estimate; excluded as an MVP predictor.
exact_locator: Perez et al., primary multivariable model/Table 3

atomic_claim: After adjustment, low-income status had odds ratio 1.00 for acceptance in the primary model.
limitations: CI includes 1; interaction model differed; excluded as an MVP predictor.
exact_locator: Perez et al., primary multivariable model/Table 3

atomic_claim: 34.1% of the national PMQ cohort reported a college laboratory research apprenticeship.
limitations: Historical PMQ respondents; participation is binary and self-reported.

atomic_claim: Among 144,473 cohort members who applied, 60.5% were accepted to medical school.
limitations: Historical cohort and PMQ-response selection; differs from all-AMCAS applicant denominator.

atomic_claim: Acceptance was 66.4% among applicants reporting a college laboratory research apprenticeship.
population: Applicants with college lab research apprenticeship
limitations: Self-selection and academic/context differences; binary exposure with no hours or output.

atomic_claim: Acceptance was 56.6% among applicants without a college laboratory research apprenticeship.
population: Applicants without college lab research apprenticeship
limitations: Self-selection and academic/context differences; denominator excludes missing data.

atomic_claim: College laboratory research apprenticeship was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.12 for acceptance.
covariates: MCAT, sex, race/ethnicity, parent education, institution type, high-school research, enrichment, honors, health-professions exposure
limitations: Historical and observational; binary participation; no hours, duration, quality, or research output.

atomic_claim: Reporting both high-school and college laboratory research was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.21 for acceptance.
predictor: Both high-school and college lab research
limitations: Historical, observational, binary exposure; cannot separate duration from selection.

atomic_claim: College summer academic enrichment participation was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.26 for acceptance.
limitations: Program participation is heterogeneous and selected; historical cohort.

atomic_claim: Honors-society participation was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.81 for acceptance.
limitations: Likely proxies academic selection/achievement; membership quality and role not measured.

atomic_claim: Health-professions exposure was associated with adjusted odds ratio 1.07 for acceptance.
limitations: Binary heterogeneous exposure; no clinical hours, responsibility, duration, or recency.

atomic_claim: First-generation graduates were less likely to apply to medical school: adjusted odds ratio 0.84.
population: College graduates in national PMQ cohort
covariates: Demographic, academic, institutional, and experiential variables specified by study
limitations: Historical cohort; context variable excluded from MVP prediction.

atomic_claim: Among applicants, first-generation graduates were less likely to be accepted: adjusted odds ratio 0.86.
covariates: Demographic, academic, institutional, and experiential variables specified by study
limitations: Historical cohort; residual confounding; context variable excluded from MVP prediction.

atomic_claim: Of 86,486 accepted cohort applicants, 84,844 (98.1%) matriculated.
population: Accepted applicants in national PMQ cohort
limitations: Historical cohort; does not indicate school choice or multiple offers.

atomic_claim: Each additional MCAT attempt was associated with odds ratio 0.85 for receiving a USUHS interview.
covariates: MCAT components, BCPM and non-BCPM GPA, military/context variables
limitations: Military-school mission, old MCAT scale, thresholded analytic sample, no extracurricular covariates.

atomic_claim: BCPM GPA was associated with odds ratio 3.65 for receiving a USUHS interview.
covariates: MCAT components, non-BCPM GPA, military/context variables
limitations: One GPA point is large; military-school mission and pre-2015 MCAT limit transportability.

atomic_claim: Non-BCPM GPA was associated with odds ratio 1.54 for receiving a USUHS interview.
covariates: MCAT components, BCPM GPA, military/context variables
limitations: Single mission-specific school; old MCAT; one GPA point is large.

atomic_claim: No prior military experience was associated with odds ratio 0.25 for a USUHS interview relative to prior military experience.
covariates: Academic and context variables in study
limitations: Reference coding is inverse of the intuitive wording; uniquely mission-specific and not transportable to civilian schools.
exact_locator: Dong et al., Table II; predictor coded as no prior military experience

atomic_claim: Self-reported disadvantaged status was not statistically associated with a USUHS interview: adjusted odds ratio 0.91.
covariates: Academic and context variables in study
limitations: Single mission-specific school; self-report; context variable excluded from MVP prediction.

atomic_claim: In the 2008 survey, MCAT scores and undergraduate GPAs were rated most important for secondary and interview invitation decisions.

limitations: Historical; mixed U.S./Canadian sample; rankings are school-reported practices, not applicant-level effects.

atomic_claim: Interview recommendations and letters of recommendation were rated most important for acceptance decisions.
population: Admissions officers at U.S. and Canadian medical schools using MCAT
limitations: Historical; school-reported importance; no standardized effect size.

atomic_claim: Among the 11 most important acceptance data types in 2008, 64% were nonacademic versus 50% in 1986.

atomic_claim: 59% (71/120) of responding schools reported conducting two interviews per interviewee.
limitations: Historical and not an admissions effect.

atomic_claim: AMCAS permits applicants to enter up to 15 experiences.

atomic_claim: AMCAS permits applicants to designate up to three experiences as most meaningful.

atomic_claim: AMCAS separates completed hours from anticipated hours.
